time_convention: t = frame / 33; frame = round(t * 33); frame 0 at t = 0
units: pixels (image coords, x right, y down, origin top-left) and seconds; no metric scale assumed

camera.motion: static (phase correlation of the building facade vs frame 0: max |shift| 0.015 px over all 99 frames; no background change outside the two movers)
camera.view: eye-level-ish view down a city street that runs away from the camera; road climbs to a crest near y~350 (sky above)

from: curb lines (left road edge and right curb) intersect near (586,194)
cyclist head-top path extrapolated to zero size: (580,208)
pedestrian head-top path extrapolated to zero size: (609,215)

camera.verticals: building edges and phone booth edges appear vertical -> little camera roll/tilt
camera.horizon_note: true horizon not visible (road crest at y~350 blocks it); the street VP above is the VP of the street direction, which rises slightly uphill
camera.focal_length: unknown; estimate from given depth_info + a known size (see notes.md)

cyclist.description: man in dark grey/black jacket and light-blue jeans riding a blue bicycle on the road, seen from behind, riding straight away from the camera up the street (left of centre)
cyclist.distinguish: the only person on a bicycle and the only one on the road; dark jacket; the other person (pedestrian) wears a white T-shirt and walks on the right sidewalk
cyclist.visible_frames: 0-98 (all); bottom of the rear wheel cut by the image bottom edge in frames 0-4
cyclist.reference_point: ref_x/ref_y = estimated rider pelvis on the saddle (torso centre line x, head_top_y + 0.44*height_smooth). A bicycle rig root would be at about ground_x/ground_y (wheel contact) or between the wheels; rider+bike are one rigid-looking unit moving together, so all these points move almost identically in direction

pedestrian.description: man in white T-shirt and light-blue jeans walking on the right-hand sidewalk away from the camera, beside the stoops / Photo Lab shop
pedestrian.distinguish: white T-shirt, on the sidewalk, walking (not cycling); right of the cyclist throughout
pedestrian.reference_point: ref_x/ref_y = estimated pelvis (hip-joint level): torso centre-line x, head_top_y + 0.47*height_smooth

apparent_height_px.note: height_px = head top to lowest foot, oscillates +-10 px with the gait

parked_bicycle.description: cream/pink ladies' bicycle with a wicker front basket parked on the LEFT sidewalk, front wheel towards camera
parked_bicycle.note: seen almost head-on; handlebar width ~ 38..150 px (~110 px); front tyre bottom at y~580, x~120

telephone_booth.description: white 'TELEPHONE' booth with cracked glass at the far end of the right sidewalk

manhole_near.description: round manhole cover in the road nearest the camera (bottom centre)
manhole_near.note: cut by bottom image edge; horizontal diameter ~267 px

manhole_far.description: second manhole cover farther up the road

tree.description: leafy street tree on the left sidewalk

photo_lab_shop.description: shop front with 'PHOTO LAB' sign, shelves of goods and a blue door with a Coca-Cola poster

stoops.description: stone stairs with railings and newel posts on the right (two big stoops in the foreground right, x 1300-1800)

railing_hedge.description: low iron railing with green hedge right of the sidewalk

right_curb.description: curb between road and right sidewalk

road.description: cobbled/asphalt street running away from the camera, cresting near y~350

sidewalks.description: light grey paved sidewalks on both sides; pedestrian walks on the right one

events.event: both movers already moving at frame 0 and keep moving through frame 98 (no start/stop, no contact between them, no direction reversal)
cyclist rear wheel fully inside the image from this frame on
pedestrian step transitions (lowest foot jumps down-image, new trailing foot); approximate, ~every 17 frames

files.tracks/cyclist.csv: final per-frame track of the cyclist
files.tracks/pedestrian.csv: final per-frame track of the pedestrian
files.tracks/*_mask.csv: raw mask statistics the final tracks are built from
